items.title: neuralopt
items.text: neuralopt tests a compact transformer policy for bounded numerical optimization alongside a deliberately restricted interval certificate system. Start with the repository README, then read the mathematical specification and limitations before using certified mode.

items.title: Held-out quadratic smoke result
items.text:
On 15 November 2026, the 100-step demo checkpoint was evaluated on three held-out four-dimensional quadratic instances (seed 42, budget 100). Median final objective was 13.0525 for the trained policy, 195.745 for random policy weights, and 2.14e-12 for SciPy L-BFGS-B with analytic JAX gradients. Median end-to-end times were 0.635 s, 0.652 s, and 0.0329 s respectively on the onboarding CPU environment. Compilation was included.

The trained policy improved on random initialization but lost decisively to the conventional baseline. This rejects H2 for this small task distribution and checkpoint. Three instances are a smoke check, not statistical evidence for H1. Raw measurements are in results/heldout-smoke.json; training loss fell from 0.260531 to 0.00994861 in 100 updates (about 12 seconds).

items.title: Hypothesis experiment plan
items.text:
All comparisons use paired task instances, seeds, dimensions, and evaluation budgets. H1 compares trained and untrained policies on held-out families and dimensions. H2 compares final and anytime regret, evaluations, failures, and wall time against an appropriate classical solver and available faithful learned baselines. H3 compares fixed widest-first branch ordering with model priority while replaying identical certificate rules. H4 records compilation, steady-state policy time, objective calls, parameter count, memory, and training cost. Ablations remove attention, history compression, gradients, low-rank factors, independent proposals, normalization augmentation, pretraining, and learned spatial guidance one factor at a time.

The bundled smoke experiment is insufficient for accepting any hypothesis: it verifies training and serialization on synthetic quadratics only.

items.title: Limitations
items.text:
This 0.1.0 research prototype has no claim of universal superiority or production maturity. The bundled training curriculum is small and supervised; it does not establish transfer beyond its sampled quadratics. Randomly initialized weights are allowed for API experimentation but are labelled as such in benchmark records. Learned stopping is emitted for research but is not used as a correctness claim.

The optimizer currently requires gradients and supports box constraints only. Residuals and nonlinear constraints are represented by the problem type but optimization rejects no constraint violations yet; they are forward-compatible metadata rather than implemented constrained optimization. Full history, curvature sketches, noise models, recurrent ablations, BBOB, MetaBox, ODE inversion, accelerator profiles, and faithful learned-optimizer baselines remain future experiments.

Certification supports an explicit expression language, not JAXPR. Its nextafter backend assumes correctly rounded host operations and libm; it is not IEEE 1788 conformant and cannot establish formal proof across arbitrary platforms. The verifier replays retained leaves but does not prove the implementation or hardware. Constraints, division, logarithms, arbitrary powers, interval Newton, Taylor models, and infeasibility proofs are unsupported and fail closed.

items.title: Literature audit
items.text: This audit informed the 0.1.0 design. Publication labels are conservative: the listed venue papers are peer reviewed; arXiv-only records are preprints unless a venue is named. Sources dated 2026 were supplied in the project brief and require bibliographic revalidation before scholarly publication.

items.title: Learned optimization
items.text:
Andrychowicz et al. (NeurIPS 2016) demonstrated coordinatewise recurrent optimizers trained by unrolling. Wichrowska et al. (ICML 2017) added hierarchical structure and broader tasks. Chen et al.'s JMLR 2022 survey formalized evaluation concerns and the gap between task-distribution success and general-purpose claims. VeLO (Metz et al., 2022 preprint) showed the value—and very large compute cost—of scale. Gärtner et al. (CVPR 2023) directly motivates attention over optimization trajectories. The NeurIPS 2022 universal hyperparameter-optimizer work uses transformers for transferable sequential decisions. B2Opt (AAAI 2025) addresses small-budget black-box search; MetaBox-v2 (2025 preprint) supplies an evolutionary-optimization benchmark ecosystem. The supplied 2026 gradient-history and Celo2 preprints are relevant recent claims, but their October 2026/arXiv and February 2026 status should be checked against canonical records before citation.

Common findings are sensitivity to training distributions, horizon truncation, feature normalization, meta-training cost, and incomplete comparisons after accounting for objective calls and wall time. Learned optimizers can exploit distributions; No Free Lunch results rule out uniform dominance over all objectives.

items.title: Representations and theory
items.text: Deep Sets establishes permutation-invariant set aggregation; Set Transformers add attention-based interactions. Von Oswald et al. (ICML 2023) construct transformer mechanisms that implement gradient-descent-like in-context updates, but this does not show that an arbitrary trained transformer discovers a robust numerical optimizer. Variable-cardinality attention, latent task tokens, coordinate permutations, normalized dimensionless features, and low-rank curvature representations are therefore useful inductive biases rather than guarantees. Bilevel unrolling provides gradients through training trajectories but creates truncation bias and memory cost. Generalization across dimension, horizon, rotations, and conditioning must be measured separately.

items.title: Certification
items.text:
Classical interval branch-and-bound derives admissible regional lower bounds, feasible upper bounds, and prunes only by proof. Natural interval extensions suffer dependency overestimation; centered forms, interval gradients/Hessians, interval Newton/Krawczyk operators, McCormick relaxations, and Taylor models can tighten bounds. IEEE 1788 specifies interval semantics and decorations; ordinary JAX/XLA arithmetic does not provide directed rounding. jax_verify propagates certified relaxations mainly for neural-network verification. jaxglobal explores JAX-oriented global optimization. Neither makes arbitrary JAX programs automatically certifiable. The supplied PNAS Nexus 2026 GPU interval-global-optimization DOI should be authenticated before its results are quoted.

The implemented backend consequently uses a tiny serializable expression subset and host binary64 nextafter expansion. It fails closed for arbitrary JAX programs. This is more limited than JAXPR interval interpretation, interval Newton, or a conforming IEEE 1788 library, but its claim is inspectable.

items.title: Evaluation
items.text: COCO/BBOB provides target-based, multi-instance benchmarking and discourages conclusions from a few analytic functions. bbob-jax helps batch/JIT evaluation, while MetaBox-v2 focuses learned evolutionary optimizers. Google learned_optimization provides tasks and learned-optimizer research infrastructure rather than a drop-in universally superior baseline. Sound studies need held-out families and instances, matched evaluation budgets, compile-time separation, paired seeds, confidence intervals, failures, and training cost.

items.title: Novelty and falsification
items.text:
The individual ingredients—transformers, learned updates, diagonal-plus-low-rank matrices, JAX, and interval branch-and-bound—are established. The candidate contribution is a compact experimental interface in which the same policy emits numerical updates and admissible search-order suggestions while certificate validity remains fully independent. This integration is a hypothesis, not established novelty or improved performance.

System family Learned direct update Variable dimension Native rigorous global bound Neural guidance can affect proof validity Evidence available here L2L / scalable recurrent optimizers Yes Varies No N/A Published studies Transformer learned optimizers Yes Varies No N/A Published studies B2Opt / MetaBox learned black-box methods Yes Often No N/A External studies SciPy/JAXopt/Optimistix No Yes No N/A Mature software Interval global solvers / jaxglobal No Yes Yes within subset N/A External software neuralopt 0.1.0 Yes Yes Yes under documented restricted assumptions No Local tests and demo only

Reported gaps in prior work include distribution shift, meta-training cost, weak wall-time accounting, unavailable weights, limited dimension/horizon transfer, and no rigorous relation between policy confidence and correctness. This package does not yet resolve them.

H1 is falsified if a trained checkpoint fails to beat its random initialization on held-out families and dimensions under paired budgets. H2 is falsified if matched SciPy and learned baselines dominate objective quality and time across the prespecified task distribution. H3 is falsified if learned ordering does not reduce median processed nodes at the same certified gap; correctness must be identical either way. H4 is falsified if inference overhead or instability erases evaluation savings, or parameter count/compute is not competitive. Gate thresholds for a larger study are: at least 20 held-out instances per family, five seeds, median regret improvement of 10% with a bootstrap 95% interval excluding zero for the claimed distribution, no increase in failure rate, and certificate replay success in every certified run.

items.title: Mathematical specification
items.text:
At step t, normalized coordinate tokens contain the current point, incumbent, scaled gradient, gradient magnitude, and availability mask. Two learned task tokens aggregate the variable-cardinality sequence. Multi-head self-attention produces coordinate states. Heads emit direction d, independent proposal q, step alpha, positive diagonal D = softplus(z)+1e-4, and low-rank U. The update is

\[x_{t+1}=\Pi_{[l,u]}(x_t+\alpha(Dd+U(U^Td))).\]

The implementation never forms the dense preconditioner. Its strict positive diagonal makes D + UUᵀ positive definite, although the learned direction does not guarantee descent. Independently evaluated proposals alternate with update candidates. A fixed reject-and-contract rule prevents propagation of worse or nonfinite candidates.

Certification uses natural interval extensions with one-ULP outward expansion after every supported operation. Branch-and-bound preserves the domain by bisection, evaluates midpoint incumbents as point intervals, and prunes only if the interval lower bound is no smaller than the feasible upper bound. Termination requires U - min_R L(R) <= epsilon. The serialized certificate retains every terminal box, including pruned boxes. Verification re-evaluates their bounds, rejects overlapping interiors, and checks exact binary-rational volume equality with the declared domain before accepting the global gap.

Assumptions: IEEE-754 binary64, correctly rounded basic NumPy operations and elementary functions supplied by the platform libm, deterministic expression semantics, compact finite boxes, and no NaNs. Since IEEE 1788 decoration and a formally verified libm are absent, certificates are validated numerical results under these assumptions, not machine-checked formal proofs.
